analysis.title: Hormuz, Hurricanes, Hikes, & Hiccups In AI's Accounting: Trump Puts War On An Election Timer As Junk Quietly Cracks
key_insights: Oil headline risk drove every asset this week. Brent traded up to about $106 intraday and WTI topped $93. Hormuz flows are about 9.5M b/d, roughly 30% below pre-war levels, and nine vessels were targeted in seven days.

Trump said the US will not attack Iran 'prior to the Midterm Elections' but left the naval blockade in place. Oil still closed up 4% on the day. Nomura's McElligott says it is '100d' that attacks resume after the votes are counted.
Goldman's Brent timespread model implies an average risk premium of $22/bbl in September, the second highest monthly reading on record after April 2026. Dated Brent rose back near post-war highs.
Brent call skew and implied vol are near the bottom of their post-March range, while the volatility of the geopolitical premium and shipping rates is rising.

Hurricane Isaias shut in about 63% of Gulf of Mexico oil output (about 1.3M b/d) and 57% of gas output (about 1.1 bcf/d). About 500K b/d of refining capacity is in its path, including Chevron's Pascagoula plant. Modeled production loss is about 9M barrels.
The 10-year Treasury yield hit about 5.36% intraday, the highest since 2002, and the 30-year printed above 5.70%. Both finished the week roughly unchanged. 2s30s topped 90bps before flattening.

Three auctions cleared well: $58B 3-year at 4.932% (through by 0.2bp), $39B 10-year at 5.300% (through by 1.7bp, indirects 80.3%, dealers a record-low 2.5%), and $22B 30-year at 5.618% (mediocre). Yields still did not fall.

Goldman's Shah says 98bp of the 108bp 10-year selloff came from real rates. Sehgal says the marginal buyer has shifted from insurers and savers to levered money that is now leaving. Buyback offers on Oct 1 were $46B against a typical $10B.

BTIG's Krinsky flagged a key reversal day in the 30-year and warns the pain trade is lower yields and a lower Nasdaq together. Deutsche Bank's Saravelos says an AI-ecosystem event is the most under-priced systemic risk and would be very bond positive.

September FOMC minutes: the Warsh Fed hiked to 3.75%-4.00% (first hike since July 2023). All 19 participants backed it and 'most' see another hike by year end as likely appropriate. December hike odds are about 80%, and October is seen as a skip at roughly one in five.

Labor data: initial claims 197K vs 200K expected, 4-week average 198K (lowest since October 2022), continuing claims 1.716M. September payrolls were only 29K. Goldman's Pasquariello stays constructive on stocks into year end provided the Fed delivers only what the strip prices.
ISM services prices paid were 74, the highest since July 2022. Goldman economists say about three-quarters of the 0.7pp core PCE overshoot reflects mismeasurement or one-offs.

French spreads reached about 160bp over Bunds, the widest since 2011, then tightened to about 140bp. The OAT was back near 4.90% by Thursday after a 2027 budget with a 5% deficit target and a record €340B borrowing requirement. Goldman's Stott says stabilizing French debt at 4% costs requires a 1% primary surplus, the 95th percentile of the last 45 years.

Contagion signs in Europe: Italy raised 2027 and 2028 deficit forecasts to 3.4% and 3.2% of GDP, Spain called a snap election for Nov 29, European banks were degrossed to April lows, and Japanese banks sold $15.9B of net foreign bonds in September.

EURUSD hit $1.1160, a 17-month low, and the dollar index reached its highest since April 2025. Goldman FX ('Fiscal Risks on Rotation') prefers currencies with intact balance sheets, namely NOK and AUD.

Brazil: Flávio Bolsonaro took 47.0% vs Lula's 45.2% in the first round. Ibovespa rose 7.7% on Monday to a record 206,912 and the real gained over 4% to below 5.00. The Jan 2031 rate future fell 97bp to 13.02%. The runoff is Oct 25, with one consultancy putting Bolsonaro at 85%.

EWZ saw a record $8B notional day and its largest weekly volume on record. Goldman recorded about $2B of foreign buying, the largest single day since 2008. The trade is now crowded ahead of an event that has not happened.

S&P 500 made its 28th record close (7,819) on Tuesday. The index is up 1.3% since Aug 27 while the S&P ex-AI is down 5.2%. Nomura counts 85% of members more than 10% below their highs and 59% more than 20% below.

The FT reported OpenAI annualized revenue near $50B at end of September, about $20B below the $68-70B figure circulating earlier. The company said the gap was gross vs net accounting for partner revenue, and Bloomberg said it expects at least $70B by year end. On the day, Nasdaq fell 1.25%, SOX 3.4%, ORCL 5.5%, AVGO 4.4%, NVDA 2.9% and CRWV 7.8%.

AI financing: Broadcom is seeking more than $50B of private debt, Oracle is negotiating an off-balance-sheet vehicle for a 1GW data center, SpaceX is assembling a $40B structure collateralized by Nvidia chips, and Tencent is lining up up to $5B. Goldman expects $420B of AI debt issuance against about $1T of net new Treasury supply.

Credit stress: Oracle 5-year CDS hit a record 261bp and Broadcom a record 136bp. CCC spreads are 1,014bp, a three-year wide and 224bp wider in three months, while IG is near 59bp and VIX is 15.4 (17th percentile of its one-year range).

Gold held around $4,160, about $300 below a month ago. Copper closed +2.1% Thursday at $6.735/lb on Chilean supply disruptions, pre-tariff stockpiling and AI/grid demand. Goldman's futures desk reports the heaviest speculative silver selling since February.

Bitcoin fell from about $87,000 to almost $80,000 before bouncing and finding support at its 50DMA. CoinGlass counted $1.09B of liquidations in 24 hours, 85% longs. Open interest stayed flat on the bounce, which points to short covering. ETF outflows were sizable.

Flows (BofA/EPFR, week to Oct 7): money market funds took in $166.4B, the most since April 2020, lifting assets to $8T. Bond funds took $33.8B (Treasuries $16.2B, a 15th straight weekly inflow). Equity funds took $12.4B globally and $3.3B in the US. Hartnett: 'no rate cuts, no cash cuts.'

market_movers.rationale: Fell 5.5% on the OpenAI revenue report. 5-year CDS hit a record 261bp, and Oracle is negotiating an off-balance-sheet vehicle for a 1GW data center.
Fell 4.4% on the week's OpenAI report. CDS hit a record 136bp, and Broadcom is seeking more than $50B of private debt to fund custom chips for OpenAI.
Fell 2.9% on the OpenAI revenue report. Nvidia processors are also collateral for a $40B SpaceX financing structure.
Fell 7.8% on the OpenAI revenue report. Neoclouds were the biggest losers in the AI complex this week.
Rose 12.5% in one session on Bolsonaro's first-round lead, with record volume and record creations. Goldman notes the trade is now crowded ahead of the Oct 25 runoff.

sector_views.rationale: AI names have lagged: the S&P ex-AI is down 5.2% since Aug 27 while the index is up 1.3%. The AI complex is the most sensitive to any challenge to the revenue story.
Energy and Utilities outperformed this week as oil stayed above $100 and Hormuz flows remain constrained.
Copper ignored the rate shock on Chilean supply disruptions, pre-tariff stockpiling and AI and grid demand.

Ticked up, which fits an economy that has stopped hiring without starting to fire.

Highest since July 2022, which supports the hawkish Fed case.

crypto_views: Bitcoin fell from about $87,000 on Tuesday to almost $80,000 on Thursday, then bounced Friday and found support at its 50DMA.
CoinGlass counted $1.09B of liquidations in 24 hours, 85% of them longs, after the long/short ratio had climbed to 1.85.
Open interest stayed flat on the bounce, which points to short covering and spot buying rather than new leverage.
Bitcoin traded like the highest-beta part of the Nasdaq during a week of fiscal alarm, which undercuts the debasement-hedge framing.
ETF holders sold, with sizable outflows in the last couple of days.
Washington moved another $1B of seized coins, which added to the weak tone.

trade_ideas.description: Own NOK and AUD against the dollar, yen and sterling, as currencies with intact balance sheets (Goldman FX, 'Fiscal Risks on Rotation')
trade_ideas.rationale: The dollar, yen and sterling all carry fiscal risk, so the cleaner expression is currencies with intact balance sheets.

risk_factors: Attacks on Iran may resume after the midterms, and Tehran has not signed up to the same calendar.
Physical oil tightness persists, and Dated Brent is near post-war highs.
Long-end Treasury yields stay high even with good auctions as the marginal buyer shifts away from insurers and savers.
Heavy AI debt issuance (about $420B) competes with about $1T of net new Treasury supply.
A failure in AI revenue growth could hit both equities and credit, since the weakest credits are at wide spreads while equity volatility is near lows.
Euro-area fiscal contagion from France to Italy and Spain.
Crowded Brazil positioning ahead of the Oct 25 runoff.
A hawkish Fed with ISM services prices paid at 74 and a labor market with no slack.
Concentration risk in AI megacaps (Deutsche Bank's Saravelos).
Reversal risk if yields and the Nasdaq fall together (BTIG).
vol_and_positioning: VIX at 15.4 sits in the 17th percentile of its one-year range, while CCC spreads are at three-year wides.
Brent call skew and implied vol are near the bottom of their post-March range, as traders unwound upside protection during the recovery in Hormuz flows.
McElligott: 'Cracks = Rate Vol', and rate vol remains elevated relative to equity's view of problems.
85% of S&P constituents are more than 10% below their highs and 59% more than 20% below. McElligott calls it a rolling correction.
Goldman traders: 6 out of 10 activity, franchise flows skewed 2% better to buy. Long-only clients skewed 1.8% to buy, hedge funds 2.4% to sell.
BTIG flagged a key reversal day in the 30-year.
EWZ saw record notional volume ($8B Monday) and its largest four-day creation on record, so the Brazil trade is crowded.
Goldman's futures desk reports the heaviest speculative silver selling since February.
Money market funds took in $166.4B, the largest weekly inflow since April 2020.
geopolitical: Iran escalated attacks around Hormuz and nine vessels were targeted in seven days.
Houthis hit Saudi airports and reportedly mined Bab al-Mandab.
Trump said the US will not attack Iran before the Midterm Elections, with the naval blockade left in place.
Reports of Pentagon strike planning surfaced Thursday.
IEA accelerated its emergency stock release.
Trump signed a diesel deal with Putin, which sent diesel lower late Friday.
Marine Le Pen unveiled a counter-budget with €140B of cuts and a constitutional golden rule.
Spain called a snap election for Nov 29.
Brazil's runoff is Oct 25 after Flávio Bolsonaro beat Lula in the first round.
Washington moved another $1B of seized crypto coins.
US midterm elections are Nov 3, and the Democratic generic-ballot lead is 8.9 points.
cross_bank_references: Goldman's Pasquariello stays constructive on stocks into year end, while Nomura's McElligott describes a rolling correction under the index.
BTIG's Krinsky sees lower yields and a lower Nasdaq as the pain trade, a tactical counterpoint to Goldman's rates desk reading of risk reduction on rallies.
Deutsche Bank's Saravelos says an AI-ecosystem event is the most under-priced risk and would be very bond positive.
Goldman economists say most of the core PCE overshoot is transitory, while the Fed minutes show most participants favor another hike.
UBS-hosted consultancy puts Bolsonaro's runoff odds at 85%.

tension_points.bull_case: Equities made 28 record closes, the OpenAI revenue gap was explained as gross vs net accounting, and Bloomberg reports OpenAI expects at least $70B by year end. Goldman's Pasquariello stays constructive into year end.
tension_points.bear_case: Oracle and Broadcom CDS are at records, CCC spreads are at three-year wides, 85% of S&P members are more than 10% below highs, and $420B of AI debt is competing with Treasury supply. Equity and credit disagree sharply.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further downward revisions to AI revenue figures, or Oracle and Broadcom CDS widening further.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman's Pasquariello expects equities to tolerate the strip's pricing of one more hike this year and about two next. Goldman economists say about three-quarters of the core PCE overshoot is mismeasurement or one-offs.
tension_points.bear_case: Most FOMC participants favor another hike, ISM services prices paid are at 74, and claims are near multi-decade lows, so there is no slack to justify a pause.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The Fed delivering more than the strip prices, which would turn it into a 'TIGHTENING CYCLE' in Pasquariello's terms.

tension_points.bull_case: Trump pledged no attacks before the midterms and the White House wants the oil risk premium gone before Nov 3.
tension_points.bear_case: McElligott says it is 100d that attacks resume after the votes are counted. Tankers were struck after the post and the blockade remains.
tension_points.what_invalidates: New attacks on shipping or a collapse of the talks before Nov 3.

tension_points.bull_case: BTIG flagged a key reversal day in the 30-year, and Deutsche Bank's Saravelos says an AI event would be very bond positive.
tension_points.bear_case: The marginal buyer has changed to levered money that is exiting, and 98bp of the selloff is from real rates despite well-received auctions.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A close above this week's highs of about 5.36% on the 10-year.
